`verus /work/ringbuffer_enqueue.rs` now prints `verification results:: 6 verified, 0 errors`.

The function body works in two cases:
- **Not full:** it writes `value` at index `(head + len) % capacity`, then increments `len`. The index is computed without the sum `head + len`, to avoid overflow.
- **Full:** it overwrites the oldest slot at `head` with `value`, then advances `head` by one, wrapping to 0 at `capacity`.

I added two helper lemmas in the proofs region. One gives `(h + l) % c` as either `h + l` or `h + l - c`. The other shows two nearby offsets from the same head never land on the same slot. The proof blocks inside the function use them to show the new view equals `old.push(value)` or `old.drop_first().push(value)`.

I only edited the `<proofs>` and `<code>` regions. I did not use `assume` or any other banned construct.
